o: The wrath of God against Israel.
Also against Jerusalem and other cities, Their precautions vain.
bg: micah, book of
The sixth in order of the so-called minor prophets. The superscription to this book states that the prophet exercised his office in the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.
Samaria
It is now represented by the hamlet of Sebustieh, containing about three hundred inhabitants. The ruins of the ancient town are all scattered over the hill, down the sides of which they have rolled.
Jacob

The history of Jacob is referred to by the prophets Hosea (12:3, 4, 12) and Malachi (1:2). In Micah 1:5 the name is a poetic synonym for Israel, the kingdom of the ten tribes. There are, besides the mention of his name along with those of the other patriarchs, distinct references to events of his life in Paul's epistles (Rom. 9:11-13; Heb. 12:16; 11:21).
Micah

"The Morasthite," so called to distinguish him from Micaiah, the son of Imlah (1 Kings 22:8). He was a prophet of Judah, a contemporary of Isaiah (Micah 1:1), a native of Moresheth of Gath (1:14, 15).
ch.s: This chapter covers: The wrath of God against Israel (vv. 1–7); Also against Jerusalem and other cities, Their precautions vain (vv. 8–16). People named: Jacob, Micah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, Achzib. Places: Jerusalem, Judah, Samaria, Gath, Aphrah.
ch.mh: The earth is called upon, with all that are therein, to hear the prophet.
q: Read verses 1–7 (The wrath of God against Israel). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 8–16 (Also against Jerusalem and other cities, Their precautions vain), what do you learn about sin and repentance?
Verse 2 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Psalms 11:4. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Jacob’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of idolatry in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Micah?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.a: Ask God to search your heart, confess what He shows you, and make any right amends.

ch.mh: Woe to the people that devise evil during the night, and rise early to carry it into execution!
q: Read verses 1–5 (The sins and desolations of Israel). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 6–11 (Their evil practices), what do you learn about prophecy and fulfillment?
Verse 1 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Psalms 36:4. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Jacob’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of the holy spirit in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Micah?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: It is not our rest: it was designed for our passage, but not for our portion; our inn, but not our home; here we have no continuing city; let us therefore arise and depart, let us seek a continuing city above.
ch.a: Ask God to search your heart, confess what He shows you, and make any right amends.

o: The birth of Christ and conversion of the Gentiles.

There are, besides the mention of his name along with those of the other patriarchs, distinct references to events of his life in Paul's epistles (Rom. 9:11-13; Heb. 12:16; 11:21).
Ephratah

The ancient name of Bethlehem in Judah (Gen. 35:16, 19; 48:7). In Ruth 1:2 it is called "Bethlehem-Judah," but the inhabitants are called "Ephrathites;" in Micah 5:2, "Bethlehem-Ephratah;" in Matt. 2:6, "Bethlehem in the land of Judah."
Nimrod
Firm, a descendant of Cush, the son of Ham. He was the first who claimed to be a "mighty one in the earth."

ch.mh: Having showed how low the house of David would be brought, a prediction of the Messiah and his kingdom is added to encourage the faith of God's people.

In verses 7–15 (The triumphs of Israel), what do you learn about judgment?

What does Jacob’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?

What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: In the mean time let us trust our Shepherd's care and power.
ch.a: Let the seriousness of God's judgment move you to examine your ways and to pray for others.

Hill of testimony, (Gen. 31:21), a mountainous region east of Jordan. From its mountainous character it is called "the mount of Gilead" (Gen. 31:25).
